frozen_before: Any export, synthesis, placement, routing or hardware-activity measurement of the step 4.4/4.5 matched control or lambda-0.3 models

amendments.reason: docs/reviews/step-4.12-independent-review.md: B1 workload/window not applicable to mapped and routed netlists; B2 no outcome after implementation failure; B3 functional gate contradicted the timed subset; N1-N8 clarifications. No hardware measurement of any new model existed when amended; the threshold, metrics, seeds and decision structure are unchanged.

docs/reviews/step-4.12-independent-review.md recheck R1: v2's core-inclusive routed rule would count step 3.9 'unclassified' interface nets (reset chain, TX, VCC, interface carries; ~529k settled changes, identical in both models) as core, diluting R toward STOP. Definition repair only; no hardware measurement of any new model existed. Routed decision now uses exactly category()=='core'. Threshold, metrics, seeds and decision structure unchanged.

purpose: Decide whether the lambda-0.3 reduction in settled logical switching is worth pursuing as an energy-saving claim, before acquiring a supported power-analysis flow.
accuracy_status: Lambda 0.3 is a hardware diagnostic only. Its step 4.5 accuracy verdicts under validation_selection_policy_v1 (1 percentage point) remain failed for seeds 1, 2 and 4 and are not changed by this rule. A PROCEED does not make lambda 0.3 a selected model. Any different accuracy allowance requires a separately named, dated policy.
threshold_scope: The 2% applies to the reduction in DLGN core switching (core nets only): a streaming-accelerator view where the core does useful work every clock. It is not a board-level percentage. On the routed UART board the core is idle most of the time; in step 3.9 core nets carried about 32,580 of 3.49 million timed board transitions (about 0.9%), so board-level reductions under the UART workload are far smaller than core reductions and are reported separately, never as the decision quantity.
threshold_rationale: Anoop's working judgement (2026-11-18) of the smallest energy saving worth pursuing. Bound in two steps: (1) if non-core power (clock, interface, I/O, static) is unchanged between models, the relative total energy reduction does not exceed the relative core energy reduction; (2) the core energy reduction is assumed not to exceed the larger of the M1/M2 reductions, i.e. per-transition energy is not systematically lower in the penalized model (M2 is only a partial check of this). Area, placement and routing differences can violate (1), so resources are reported alongside.

models.note: Seed-0 lambda-0.3 is the step 4.4 sweep model, not the step 4.3 lambda-0.1 penalty run. Archived checkpoints and model.json files; no retraining. Split seed 0 throughout.

fixed_setup.workload: All 270 saved validation images (x_validation_bits.npy) in saved order, identical bytes and schedule for every model. Standalone head-only core runs (probe and zero-delay mapped metrics): one image per clock after reset, as step 3.8. Routed UART-board runs: one clean request per image at the hardware 104-clock divider with the step 3.9 testbench request spacing. Test data are not loaded for inference, export or simulation.

window.standalone_core: (first input drive - half period - 1 ps, last output check], as step 3.8; i.e. (first_input_ps - 41667 - 1, last_output_check_ps] from the validated event ledger.
window.routed_uart_board: (rising clock edge before the first request start bit, last reply stop bit + one clock period]. Bounds are fixed in clock cycles by the schedule, so they are identical for both models of a pair, and include all post-edge settling and glitches.

fixed_setup.architecture: Feasible head-only core: layer_pipeline false, head_pipeline true (LAT 3)
fixed_setup.constraints: Unchanged step 2.7 SDC/PCF for routed board experiments; constraints are never relaxed.
fixed_setup.functional_gate: Every model must match its own NumPy integer scores and lowest-index argmax for all 270 images in RTL, in zero-delay simulation of its mapped netlist and in zero-delay simulation of each routed netlist. Each timed simulation must also match on every image it simulates. No activity value counts before these checks pass.

implementation_failure: If any primary model fails the functional gate, fit/packing, routing or the 12 MHz timing check on any placement seed, its available metrics are reported and the final outcome is INCONCLUSIVE (implementation failure), never STOP or PROCEED. A correctness fix to project code is rerun on every model of every affected pair. Constraints are never relaxed. In the probe, a functional mismatch or a non-positive control metric yields no PAUSE/CONTINUE until fixed, and fixed code is rerun on both models.

core_definition.standalone_core: Nets driven by mapped LUT4, carry and flip-flop cells (step 3.8 ledger categories lut, carry, ff): input register, logic layers, score adders, head score registers, argmax/output registers and valid-chain flip-flops (identical in both models). Excluded: clock, reset and in_valid primary inputs, the x input port nets and testbench signals.
core_definition.routed_uart_board: Step 3.9 rule (scripts/capture_timed_activity.py category()): a net is core if a visible name starts with 'board.adapter.core.'. The decision uses exactly the nets with category() == 'core'. Nets classified 'unclassified', 'interface', 'clock', 'global_buffer' or 'io' are excluded from the decision and reported separately by name and count. As a sensitivity check only, M1/M2 are also reported with the board.adapter.core.out_valid_* nets moved to interface. The classification code hash is recorded with each result.

metrics.M1_raw: Sum over core nets of known 0/1 transitions within the window. X/Z-involving changes are counted separately and must be zero inside the window.
metrics.M2_fanout_weighted: Sum over core nets of known transitions multiplied by the net's fanout: the number of mapped cell input-pin bits the net drives in the analysed netlist (not its own driver, not top-level port references). Rough capacitance stand-in only; not calibrated capacitance, wire length or energy. Mapped-netlist M2 is not comparable with routed-netlist M2.

reduction: R = 1 - penalty_value / control_value for each metric and model seed, computed with each model's mean over its placement seeds where placement applies.

screening_probe.pair: Model seed 1 (first primary repeat seed; smallest logical reduction of the primary seeds, 16.04%)
screening_probe.netlist: Zero-delay post-synthesis mapped simulation of the standalone head-only core (step 3.8 style). Deterministic synthesis; no placement seed. Synthesis resource counts are reported; packing/fit is not established by the probe (standalone core ports exceed SG48 pins).
screening_probe.tooling: Validation-vector export, mapped capture of new models, core-net and fanout counting belong to step 4.13 (scripts/probe_mapped_switching.py). Step 4.14 zero-delay mapped M1/M2 reuse that code unchanged.

decision.PAUSE: R < 2% on both M1 and M2. Do not build steps 3.11/4.14; record and discuss with the professor. Not the final STOP.
decision.CONTINUE: R >= 2% on M1 or M2. Build steps 3.11 and 4.14 and apply the final rule.

screening_probe.after_pause: Resuming 3.11/4.14 after a PAUSE requires a new, dated, separately named policy; the threshold may not be reinterpreted after the fact.
screening_probe.limits: One seed and no glitches; synthesis may remove constant gates differently for the two models. The probe cannot establish the final decision in either direction.

final_rule.secondary_reason: Seed 0 informed the choice of lambda 0.3 and is reported separately, not averaged into the primary result.
final_rule.netlist: Routed head-only UART board design with SDF back-annotated delays (step 3.9 style), core nets only.
final_rule.placement_evidence: Record each placement's .asc hash; identical hashes for different seeds are reported, so zero noise can be distinguished from repeated placements.
final_rule.timed_image_set: N = min(270, max(32, floor(B / t_image))), with budget B = 1800 s of timed-simulation wall time per run and t_image measured on the seed-1 control, placement seed 1, before any lambda-0.3 timed result is produced. N is then fixed for every timed run; images are the first N in saved order. Zero-delay mapped M1/M2 on all 270 images are reported for every model regardless.
final_rule.noise: Per metric. For each model, placement range = max - min over its placement seeds. Pair noise = larger of the two models' ranges. Primary noise = mean pair noise over seeds 1-4.
decision_order: INCONCLUSIVE (implementation failure): any condition in implementation_failure.
STOP: mean primary R < 2% on both M1 and M2. Stop the energy-saving framing; use the characterization framing.

PROCEED: for at least one metric, mean primary R >= 2% and mean (control - penalty) difference > 2 x that metric's primary noise. Proceed to a supported power flow (5.x). PROCEED is not an energy claim.
INCONCLUSIVE: anything else. Report, do not claim a hardware switching reduction, discuss next steps.
final_rule.descriptive_only: Also report how many primary seeds individually have R >= 2% per metric, so one outlier seed cannot hide behind the mean. This count does not change the decision.

always_report: Per-seed and per-placement M1/M2, R, LUT4, flip-flops, carry cells, packed cells, fit, routed Fmax and 12 MHz pass/fail; board-level transition totals under the UART workload separately from core totals. A model that fails to fit or meet timing is recorded as such, never dropped or rerouted under different constraints.
limits: Every metric here is a switching proxy. None is power or energy. Icarus timing filters narrow pulses inertially and uses one delay corner. Passing does not establish an energy reduction, novelty or venue suitability; failing does not invalidate the verified logical-switching result.
